intro:
Use it to give other people access to one document, board or file. The panel puts the job in the order it is done: who to add, who already has access, and the two ways to send it, an invitation or the link.

Addresses typed into the field become chips, so several can be invited at once with one role. Sending and copying answer in the button that was pressed, which keeps its width while its label changes.

It opens as a popover beside its trigger, or with `presentation="dialog"` in the middle of the screen. For a dialog with a different job, use [Dialog](/docs/web/components/dialog).
usage:
<Share link={url} onInvite={({ emails, role }) => invite(emails, role)}>
  <Share.Trigger people={members} />
  <Share.Content title="Share “Spring lookbook”">
    <Share.Invite roles={ROLES} />
    <Share.People>
      {members.map((member) => (
        <Share.Person key={member.email} name={member.name} role={member.role} />
      ))}
    </Share.People>
    <Share.Footer>
      <Share.CopyLink />
      <Share.Send />
    </Share.Footer>
  </Share.Content>
</Share>

parts.Trigger: The pill that opens it. `people` draws up to three faces at its start, so the button also says who has access already.
parts.Content: The panel and the band around it. `title` is the heading and what the panel is announced as. The close button is drawn for you.
parts.Invite: The field for addresses. Each one becomes a chip after Enter, a comma or a space, and Backspace in an empty field takes the last one back. `roles` sets the select at its end.
parts.RoleSelect: The compact role select used in the field and beside each person. Use it on its own for a role select of your own.
parts.Access: A row saying who can open it from the link alone, with a select of levels.
parts.People: Who already has access, under a heading. `label` changes the heading.
parts.Person: One person: initials or picture, name, an optional second line, and their role. With `roles` and `onRoleChange`, the role is a select.
parts.Footer: The buttons, as equal pills in the band under the panel, wherever it is written.
parts.CopyLink: Copies `link` and says "Copied" for a moment.
parts.Send: Calls `onInvite`. It shows Sending while the returned promise is pending, then Sent, then clears the field.

examples.title: As a dialog
examples.description:
`presentation="dialog"` opens the panel in the middle of the screen over a dimmed page. Use it when sharing is reached from a menu rather than from a button of its own.

`Share.Access` adds a row for who can open it from the link alone.

examples.title: Changing roles
examples.description:
Give `Share.Person` the `roles` and an `onRoleChange`, and its role becomes a select. A role that cannot change, such as an owner's, is given as text with no `roles`.

A footer with only `Share.CopyLink` suits a panel for managing access rather than adding to it.

notes:
### Sending

`onInvite` is called with `{ emails, role }`. Everyone chipped in the field is included, and so is a complete address still being typed. Return a promise to keep the button spinning until it settles. When it resolves, the button shows Sent and the field is cleared. When it rejects, the button goes back to Send and the addresses stay, so they can be sent again.

Adding the new people to `Share.People` is up to you. The first example does it in `onInvite`.

### The keyboard

Enter in the field turns the typed address into a chip. Enter in an empty field sends. Escape closes the panel and returns focus to the trigger.

### Screen readers

The panel is announced by its title. Both buttons announce what happened, "Invitation sent" and "Link copied", through a live region. Each person's role select is named for them, as "Role for Ines Duarte".
